## Function Archive Run

Writes .morph/runs/<runId>/ (deck.json, report.json, answers/ committed with Morph-Run trailers; requests/ ignored); append-only.

Behaviour: archiveRun(root, {runId, deck, report, answers?}, env): runId must match ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$, else {ok: false, error: "invalid runId: <runId>"}; an answer whose request.customId does not match it → {ok: false, error: "invalid answer id: <customId>"} (the first such, in order). dir = ".morph/runs/<runId>"; an existing root/dir → {ok: false, error: "archive <dir> already exists"} (a run id names one run forever). A refusal writes nothing. Else mkdir -p, write <dir>/deck.json = JSON.stringify(deck.cards, null, 2) + "\n" (the Deck File form, a JSON array of cards) and <dir>/report.json = JSON.stringify(report, null, 2) + "\n". Then, answers not empty: <dir>/requests/.gitignore = "*\n" and per answer in order <dir>/requests/<customId>.request.json.gz = gzipSync (node:zlib) of JSON.stringify(request, null, 2) + "\n" — the request copies repeat the slices: kept on disk, ignored in any repo, never committed — and, when text is not null, <dir>/answers/<customId>.answer.txt = text exactly; then <dir>/answers/lines.txt = the answers' lines concatenated in order, when any answer has a line. answers absent or [] → no answers/ and no requests/. Then Commit Paths over [<dir>/deck.json, <dir>/report.json, the answer.txt files in order, answers/lines.txt] with subject "morph run <runId>: deck and report" and trailers Morph-Run <runId>, Morph-Cards <deck.cards.length>, Morph-Written, Morph-Failed, Morph-Skipped, Morph-Budget-Exceeded (the number of report.outcomes with that status). → {ok: true, dir, commit: the sha, or null when Commit Paths returned null}. A git failure of the commit (an ignored .morph/ makes git add refuse) → {ok: false, error: "archive <dir> written but not committed: <the Error's message>"}; the files stay on disk. saveBatchRecord(root, record) (exported; record {batchId, …}, a Batch Record) writes <root>/.morph/batches/<batchId>.json = JSON.stringify(record, null, 2) + "\n" (mkdir -p; local state, not committed) and returns ".morph/batches/<batchId>.json"; a batchId outside ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ → null, nothing written.

Steps:
- reads: Deck
- reads: Run Report
- calls: Commit Paths
- produces: Archive Result

Data Deck: The loaded backlog.
Schema:
{
  "cards": "Card[] in file order",
  "externalDependsOn": "string[] — dependsOn names not in the deck"
}

Data Run Report: The summary of one run (its schema and archive layout are runloop's; the file write and commit are P6 git's).
Schema:
{ runId: string, completedAt: number, branch: string, processor: string, generations: number, outcomes: CardOutcome[], usageTotals: { inputTokens: number, outputTokens: number, cost: number | null, requests: number }, requests?: RequestUsage[] } — requests is always set by Run Deck; it is optional in the type so a report literal built elsewhere stays valid

Data Archive Result: The archive written and committed, or the refusal.
Schema:
{ ok: true, dir: string, commit: string | null } | { ok: false, error: string }

## Function Read Batch

One reply about a batch (status + body text) into a Batch Read.

Behaviour: readBatch(status, text) is pure, never throws. Status outside 200..299 → state "error", error "http <status>: <the JSON body's error.message, else the text's first 200 chars>"; a 2xx body not a JSON object → "unreadable response: <first 200 chars>"; no string status → "provider error: <error.message, else 'no batch status'>"; an error read has batchId null, status null, replies []. ## Function Read Registry

MORPH_PROCESSOR_<id>_* env vars into Processor Configs; faults listed, never dropped silently.

## Function Run Deck

Generations in order (layerGenerations), budget checked at each generation boundary (maxCards, deadline), retries budgeted per card (2) and capped per generation (maxRetryBatches), the Run Report produced at the end.

Behaviour: runDeck(input, deps) runs input.deck generation by generation in the order of layerGenerations(input.deck). At each generation boundary it checks the budget: deps.now() >= input.budget.deadline → every not-yet-done card of this and the later generations becomes {status: "budget-exceeded", reason "deadline"}; cardsProcessed >= input.budget.maxCards → reason "maxCards <maxCards>". Otherwise it resolves the runnable cards (resolveRunnable with the statuses so far), records the skipped outcomes, runs processGeneration on the runnable cards, accumulates their usage and request rows, keeps the Retry Context of every failed card (by its original id; a later round's context replaces an earlier one), and adds the runnable count to cardsProcessed. A card that failed is retried: the budget is per card — every card may be retried 2 times, in whichever generation it runs — and input.budget.maxRetryBatches caps the retry batches of ONE generation: retryBatches starts at 0 at every generation, and while some failed card has been retried fewer than 2 times and retryBatches < maxRetryBatches, a retry batch runs (retryBatches += 1) for all such cards (a card of an earlier generation whose retries the cap stopped is included), unless deps.now() >= the deadline, checked before each retry batch: then each such card becomes its outcome with status "budget-exceeded", reason "deadline", and no retry batch runs. A batch: buildRetry(original card, retryNumber, the card's latest Retry Context acceptanceOutput, its previousDiff) for each, processGeneration on the retries, and a retry that is written updates the card's outcome (status "written", its commit, attempts = the retry number + 1) while every attempt's log is appended to earlierFailures. At the end it builds the Run Report: runId, completedAt = deps.now(), branch = input.branch, processor = deps.config.id, generations = the generation count, outcomes in deck order, usageTotals {inputTokens, outputTokens summed; cost the sum of the reported costs or null when none was reported; requests = the number of usage rows}, requests = every Request Usage row of every processGeneration call of the run, in send order. Returns {report, outcomes}. deps reach every processGeneration call as given (so deps.onVariant also sees the retries' variants). It writes and commits nothing.

Steps:

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response, Stub Answer, Assemble Batch and Read Batch are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation and Send Batch (P4, P11). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b).
- Node Only: Runtime dependencies: Node 20 built-ins and the package `yaml` (the record reader), nothing else; dev dependencies pinned exactly, no ^ or ~.

Guardrails:
- No Network In Tests: tests/setup.ts makes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and net.connect throw "network blocked in tests"; only the processor's own transport is mocked.
- No Shell Outside Acceptance: child processes are spawned only by Run Acceptance, the git module (in Run Git alone, P6) and the processor's none; everything else is pure.
- Frozen Tree During Run: while a run is in flight no file outside the cards' targets and .morph/ changes; a changed declared input discards the answer unread.

Callee Commit Paths: Stages exactly the given paths and commits them with a subject and trailers; null when nothing changed.
Behaviour: commitPaths(root, paths, subject, trailers, env): `git add -A -- <paths>`; `git diff --cached --name-only -- <paths>` empty → null, no commit. Else `git commit -q -m <subject> -m <trailer block> -- <paths>`, the trailer block being one "<key>: <value>" line per trailer in the given order joined by "\n" (hooks run; nothing is bypassed), so the message is "<subject>\n\n<trailer lines>". Only the paths are committed: a file staged by hand or modified outside them stays as it was. Then commit = `git rev-parse HEAD` (trimmed) and the diffstat from `git show --numstat --format= <commit>`: files = the number of non-empty lines, insertions and deletions the sums of the first two columns ("-" for a binary file counts 0). Returns Commit Info.

## Function Send Batch

One generation as one OpenRouter batch - submit once, poll, map the results back.

Behaviour: sendBatch(config, requests, transport) never rejects; answers and usage in the order of requests, one each; exports BATCH_POLL_MS 15000, BATCH_GRACE_MS 60000. A request whose model is set and is not config.model is answered "batch runs one model: <customId> pins <model>, the batch is <config.model>" on every path and left out; none left → no call. Submit: Assemble Batch of the rest, ONE transport.fetch(url, {method POST, headers, body}), never retried (maybe a paid batch already), then Read Batch: thrown → every request "batch submit: transport: <message>"; an error read → "batch submit: <its error>"; no batchId → "batch submit: no batch id" (no batch key in any of these results). Then the Batch Record {batchId, processor: config.id, model: config.model, customIds: the submitted ids, status: the submit's, cost: null} goes to transport.saveBatch when set (a throw ignored). Poll k = 1..polls, polls = max(1, floor(timeoutMs / BATCH_POLL_MS)): transport.sleep(BATCH_POLL_MS), then transport.fetch(url + "/" + batchId, {method GET, headers}), no body, then Read Batch. A thrown poll, status 408, 429, 5xx, and a 404 while k × BATCH_POLL_MS ≤ BATCH_GRACE_MS go on; any other error read is final: every request "batch <batchId>: <its error>". A read's status and cost update the record; pending → next poll; done or failed → saveBatch again, each request takes the first reply with its customId, else "batch <batchId> <status>: <the batch's error, else 'no result'>"; when the read has a cost and no reply has one, each reply's cost = Math.round(cost * (inputTokens + outputTokens) / total * 1e10) / 1e10, total the replies' tokens summed (0 → null). Polls run out → the batch is cancelled: ONE transport.fetch(url + "/" + batchId, {method DELETE, headers}), no body (a 2xx sets the record's status "deleted"; a throw or any other reply is ignored), saveBatch again, then every request "batch <batchId> still <the last status a poll read> after <polls> polls". An error answer has text and finishReason null, usage 0, 0 and nulls. Once a batch id exists every result carries batch, a copy of the record.
